questions.q: The 1999 Constitution requires most withdrawals from the Consolidated Revenue Fund of the Federation for government expenditure to be authorised through
options: an appropriation law passed by the National Assembly
a directive of the President published in the Federal Gazette
a warrant issued by the Accountant-General of the Federation without statutory authority
a resolution of the National Economic Council
questions.explanation: Withdrawals for government expenditure are controlled by the legislature through the appropriation law, commonly called the budget. The President may implement the budget and the Accountant-General may issue warrants, but neither can create the constitutional authority to withdraw funds from the Consolidated Revenue Fund.

questions.q: A serving state governor is accused of an offence allegedly committed before he assumed office. Under the 1999 Constitution, which statement best reflects the position while he remains in office?
options: He can be prosecuted only after the State House of Assembly passes a vote of no confidence.
He must be immediately tried by a magistrate court in the state capital.
He may not be prosecuted while still serving as governor, but the immunity ends when he leaves office.
He is permanently immune from prosecution after completing his tenure.
questions.explanation: The Constitution grants sitting presidents, vice-presidents, governors and deputy governors immunity from criminal proceedings during their tenure. The immunity is temporary and does not wipe out the alleged offence, so prosecution may be commenced after the governor leaves office.

questions.q: Two political parties in Oyo State agree not to merge, but to support the same governorship candidate and jointly campaign for him in the 2027 election. This arrangement is best described as
questions.explanation: A coalition is an alliance of parties that retain their separate identities while cooperating for an electoral or governmental purpose. A merger would fuse them into one party, whereas a caucus is an internal group and a referendum is a public vote.

questions.q: A newly formed association of market women in Aba wants the state government to reduce multiple taxation. Which action is most consistent with its role as a pressure group?
options: sponsoring candidates for every ward in the local government election
lobbying the State House of Assembly and presenting a memorandum on taxation
forming a government after winning the majority of seats
registering members to contest under a party platform
questions.explanation: Pressure groups seek to influence public policy without taking over government, and lobbying legislators plus submitting a memorandum is a standard method. Sponsoring candidates, forming a government, and contesting under a party platform are functions of political parties rather than pressure groups.

questions.q: A revolutionary government controls the capital, collects taxes and is generally obeyed within a West African state, but other states refuse to recognise it diplomatically. In political science, the government most clearly has
options: both de facto and de jure sovereignty
de jure sovereignty without de facto sovereignty
neither de facto nor de jure sovereignty
de facto sovereignty without de jure sovereignty
questions.explanation: De facto sovereignty refers to actual effective control over a territory and its people, while de jure sovereignty refers to lawful or recognised status. Since the government controls and is obeyed but lacks diplomatic recognition, it exercises de facto rather than de jure sovereignty.

questions.q: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control exercises powers given to it by an Act of the National Assembly. Its authority is best described as
questions.explanation: The agency's powers are conferred by statute and are therefore limited and revocable by the legal framework that created them. It does not possess sovereign authority, which belongs to the state, nor does its power rest on custom or personal charisma.

questions.q: The treaty that formally established the Economic Community of West African States in 1975 is known as the
options: Charter of the Organisation of African Unity
questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States was established by the Treaty of Lagos in 1975. The Abuja Treaty later provided for an African Economic Community, while the Lomé Convention dealt with trade and aid relations and the OAU Charter established the Organisation of African Unity.

questions.q: The Assembly of the African Union is made up mainly of
options: Permanent Representatives of member states to the African Union
Heads of State and Government of member states
Ministers of Foreign Affairs of member states
Speakers of national parliaments of member states
questions.explanation: The Assembly is the African Union's supreme organ and is composed of heads of state and government of member states. Foreign ministers sit in the Executive Council, while permanent representatives form the Permanent Representatives Committee.

questions.q: Which United Nations specialised agency is primarily responsible for setting international labour standards?
options: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
questions.explanation: The International Labour Organization is the UN specialised agency that promotes decent work and sets international labour standards. The World Health Organization handles public health, UNESCO handles education and culture, while FAO deals with food and agriculture.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: In Nigeria, the constitutional separation of legislative, executive and judicial powers is mainly intended to
options: make all public officials belong to the same political party
place the judiciary under the direct control of the executive
enable the National Assembly to conduct elections for the President
prevent the concentration of governmental power in one person or body
questions.explanation: Separation of powers divides authority among the legislature, executive and judiciary so that no single organ can exercise absolute power. Placing the judiciary under the executive would undermine, rather than promote, this principle.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The power of the President of Nigeria to grant pardon to a convicted person is best described as
options: a legislative check on the executive
a judicial review of executive action
an executive check on the judiciary
a judicial check on the legislature
questions.explanation: The prerogative of mercy allows the President to pardon or reduce a sentence, thereby serving as an executive check on decisions of the courts. Judicial review, by contrast, is exercised by courts to examine the legality of actions or laws.

questions.q: Under the Clifford Constitution of 1922, the legislative council was empowered to make laws for
options: the whole of Nigeria, including the Northern Provinces
the Colony of Lagos and the Southern Provinces
the Colony of Lagos and the Northern Provinces
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution created a legislative council whose authority covered the Colony of Lagos and the Southern Provinces, while the Northern Provinces were administered separately. Extending its powers to the whole of Nigeria or to the Northern Provinces confuses it with later constitutional arrangements.

questions.q: Under Nigerian federalism, matters not listed in the exclusive and concurrent legislative lists are within the legislative competence of
options: local government councils as constitutionally independent law-making bodies
state governments acting through their Houses of Assembly
questions.explanation: Such matters are residual and are reserved to the states, whose Houses of Assembly may legislate on them. Local governments exercise functions delegated by state law rather than independent constitutional law-making powers.

questions.q: A system in which a hereditary ruler reigns as head of state but effective political power is exercised within constitutional limits is known as
questions.explanation: In a constitutional monarchy the monarch’s role is limited by law and political power is exercised through constitutional institutions. An absolute monarchy lacks such legal limits, while an oligarchy is rule by a small group.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a unitary system of government?
options: A central government may create or abolish local authorities and delegate functions to them
Component units have a constitutionally guaranteed right to secede
Local governments have residual powers not assigned to the centre
Powers are shared between central and regional governments under a written constitution
questions.explanation: In a unitary system, legal sovereignty rests with the central government, which can reorganize local authorities and assign them functions. Shared constitutional powers with regions and residual powers for local units are features associated with federal arrangements.

questions.q: The electoral system in which a candidate who obtains an absolute majority of first-preference votes wins immediately, but if no one does, the lowest candidate is eliminated and preferences are transferred until a winner emerges is known as
questions.explanation: The alternative vote uses preference transfers after eliminating the weakest candidate when no first-preference majority exists. First-past-the-post elects the plurality winner without transfers, and a two-round system uses a separate second ballot rather than transfer of preferences.

questions.q: In a governorship election in Kogi State, which has 21 local government areas, a candidate is constitutionally required to score at least one-quarter of the votes cast in how many local government areas?
questions.explanation: The Constitution requires at least one-quarter of the votes cast in at least two-thirds of the local government areas. Two-thirds of 21 is 14, so the candidate must meet that spread requirement in 14 local government areas. One-third would be 7, while 11 is below the required two-thirds.

questions.q: The main purpose of the secret ballot in Nigerian elections is to
options: reduce the cost of voter registration
protect voters from intimidation and keep their choices confidential
make voters announce their choices publicly
allow party agents to verify how each voter voted
questions.explanation: The secret ballot protects the voter’s choice from intimidation, bribery and victimization after voting. Requiring voters to disclose their choices or allowing agents to verify them would defeat that protection.

questions.q: Which military Head of State introduced the Operation Feed the Nation programme in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Operation Feed the Nation was launched in 1976 under General Olusegun Obasanjo to encourage food production. It is not associated with Gowon, Murtala Mohammed or Babangida, although those names are connected with other Nigerian military governments.

questions.q: The military regime of General Sani Abacha created how many states in Nigeria in 1996?
questions.explanation: In 1996, the Abacha military government created six new states: Bayelsa, Ebonyi, Ekiti, Gombe, Nasarawa and Zamfara. This increased the number of states in Nigeria to thirty-six.

questions.q: A State government wants to know how residents feel about a proposed ₦2,000 transport levy. It commissions a survey of a representative sample of residents. This method is best described as
questions.explanation: An opinion poll measures public views by surveying a representative sample of people. A referendum or plebiscite requires the electorate to vote directly on an issue, while a general election is for choosing representatives.

questions.q: Which statement best describes public opinion?
options: The total number of people who voted in the last election
The personal view of a government official on official matters
The view held by a significant section of the public on issues of general concern
The decision reached by a court in a landmark case
questions.explanation: Public opinion refers to the views held by a significant section of the public on matters of general concern. It is not merely the private view of an official, a court judgment, or a record of voter turnout.

questions.q: Which court has original jurisdiction over a dispute between the Federal Government of Nigeria and a State?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court has original jurisdiction under the Nigerian Constitution in disputes between the Federation and a state or between states. Other courts do not have original jurisdiction in such constitutional disputes at first instance.

questions.q: The existence of several political parties competing for power in Nigeria is best described as a
questions.explanation: A multi-party system exists where several political parties are free to compete for power and can win offices. Nigeria has many registered parties, unlike a one-party or two-party system.

questions.q: A group of traders in Aba sends representatives to meet members of the State House of Assembly to argue against a new market levy. This method of influencing government is called
questions.explanation: Lobbying involves pressure groups or their representatives directly persuading legislators or public officials on a proposed policy. Picketing is a form of public protest, while a referendum is a direct vote and an electoral campaign is aimed at winning elections.

questions.q: A director in the Lagos State civil service issues a circular, and subordinates comply because the civil service regulations empower the director's office to issue such instructions. Which type of authority is illustrated?
questions.explanation: Legal-rational authority rests on accepted rules and the office held, not on the person's inherited status or personal appeal. Subordinates comply because the civil service regulations authorise the director's office to issue the circular; coercion is not the basis described.

questions.q: A group takes over a state's radio station and government buildings and uses soldiers to compel obedience. Many citizens obey only from fear, while foreign governments continue to recognise the ousted administration. Which conclusion best follows?
options: The ousted administration still has effective power because it is recognised abroad.
The group has traditional authority because it controls government buildings.
The group has effective power but lacks legitimacy.
The group has legitimate authority because it controls the army.
questions.explanation: Legitimacy is about acceptance or rightfulness, not merely control of coercion. Recognition of the ousted administration abroad does not by itself restore its effective power, while fear-based obedience shows power without legitimacy.

questions.q: Which situation best shows that sovereignty can be limited in practice even when a state is legally independent?
options: A state governor appoints commissioners to head ministries.
The Supreme Court interprets a section of the constitution.
Nigeria signs a treaty and later finds that its tariff policy is restricted by the agreement.
The National Assembly debates a bill on petroleum taxation.
questions.explanation: A state may be legally sovereign but voluntarily accept treaty obligations that constrain specific policy choices. Domestic legislative, executive and judicial actions do not by themselves show an external limitation on sovereignty.

questions.q: Under the ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, a citizen of a member state may normally enter another member state without a visa for a period of up to
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS free movement regime grants community citizens visa-free entry for up to 90 days. Longer stays may require residence or establishment procedures under the relevant protocols.

questions.q: The day-to-day administrative work of the United Nations is carried out by the
questions.explanation: The Secretariat, headed by the Secretary-General, administers United Nations programmes and services. The other organs have specific deliberative, enforcement or judicial roles.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: A bill approved by the House of Representatives cannot become law until it is also passed by the Senate and presented to the President. This arrangement illustrates
options: the complete separation of the legislature from the executive
the exclusive law-making power of the upper chamber
the fusion of legislative and executive powers
checks and balances among government organs
questions.explanation: The two chambers check each other, and presidential assent or refusal adds another check. It is not fusion, because each organ retains distinct functions and can check the others.

questions.q: The policy of 'citizen diplomacy' in Nigeria's foreign policy is mainly concerned with
options: granting automatic citizenship to all Africans in Nigeria
restricting Nigerian citizens from travelling abroad
making foreign policy solely through the United Nations
protecting the welfare and interests of Nigerians abroad
questions.explanation: Citizen diplomacy focuses on the Nigerian citizen abroad, including protection, welfare and diaspora engagement. It does not confer citizenship on foreigners or prevent Nigerians from travelling abroad.

questions.q: Nigeria's membership of the African Union is most consistent with which foreign policy objective?
options: Making the African Union superior to Nigeria's constitution
Avoiding all forms of foreign economic relations
Establishing military bases in every African state
questions.explanation: Nigeria's Afrocentric foreign policy supports continental unity and cooperation, including through the African Union. Membership does not erase Nigeria's sovereignty or constitution, nor does it require military bases or economic isolation.

questions.q: The preamble of a constitution is important mainly because it
options: sets out the broad aims and aspirations of the people
prescribes the procedure for removing public officers
lists the matters on which state governments may legislate
contains the fundamental human rights enforceable in court
questions.explanation: The preamble introduces the constitution by stating the ideals, purposes and aspirations of the people. It is not the section that normally contains enforceable rights, legislative lists or removal procedures.

questions.q: In Nigeria's federal system, the National Economic Council is primarily responsible for
options: settling disputes between the federal and state governments
advising the President on the economic affairs of the Federation
questions.explanation: The National Economic Council includes the Vice-President, state governors and key economic officials, and its core function is to advise the President on economic affairs and coordination. Disputes between governments are handled through legal channels such as the courts, while ministerial appointments and census matters belong to other bodies.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, local government councils in Nigeria derive their existence and functions mainly from
options: laws made by state houses of assembly
questions.explanation: The Constitution places the system of local government under state governments and requires each state to provide for local councils through a state law. This makes state houses of assembly the main lawmakers for local government structure and functions, except for the Federal Capital Territory.

questions.q: A form of government in which the state seeks to control every aspect of public and private life and tolerates no organised opposition is called
questions.explanation: Totalitarianism is marked by extensive state control over public and private life and the suppression of organised opposition. Constitutionalism and constitutional monarchy limit governmental power, while federalism is a territorial division of power rather than total control.

questions.q: The deliberate redrawing of constituency boundaries to concentrate the supporters of one political party in selected areas is called
questions.explanation: Gerrymandering is the manipulation of constituency boundaries to give a party or group an unfair advantage. Malapportionment refers to unequal population sizes among constituencies, while franchise is the right to vote.

questions.q: A child born in London to Mr and Mrs Adeyemi, both of whom are Nigerian citizens, acquires Nigerian citizenship by
questions.explanation: Nigerian citizenship by descent covers a person born outside Nigeria where either parent is a Nigerian citizen. Naturalization and registration are other routes for persons who are not Nigerian by birth or descent.

questions.q: A public opinion poll is most likely to give an unreliable picture of national opinion when
options: respondents are selected randomly from the population
the findings are published in newspapers
the sample is small and unrepresentative of the population
the poll is conducted before an election
questions.explanation: The credibility of a poll depends largely on a sample that is adequate and representative of the group being studied. A small or biased sample can produce results that do not reflect the wider population, even if the poll is conducted before an election or reported in newspapers.
